detail.transcript: I had a really long day at work today and I keep replaying that conversation with my manager in my head.
detail.reply: It sounds like your mind is still running over that moment. Did you feel heard during the conversation, or was there something you wished you’d said?

detail.transcript: I don't really know why I've been feeling so flat this week. Nothing is wrong exactly, it just all feels like effort.
detail.reply: It’s strange how small things can feel like work when everything else seems normal. Have you noticed anything specific that made you feel this way, even if it wasn’t a big deal?

detail.transcript: I finally finished the thing I had been putting off for a month and I feel a lot lighter than I expected to.
detail.reply: That’s beautiful. You did it. How did it feel when the last part came together?

detail.transcript: My sister called and we ended up arguing about the same thing we always argue about, and I hung up feeling like the bad guy.
detail.reply: You let yourself feel like the bad guy again. That’s heavy. What did you argue about this time?

detail.transcript: I have been sleeping badly for about two weeks now and I think it is making everything feel harder than it actually is.
detail.reply: I hear how hard this has been. It sounds like sleep has been a struggle, and that’s making everything feel heavier. How have you been trying to rest?

detail.transcript: I cried in the bathroom at work today and I genuinely do not know what set it off.
detail.reply: It’s okay to cry when something feels too heavy to name. Did anything feel familiar about the moment, even if you can’t put words to it?

detail.transcript: My grandmother died last month and I still cannot talk about it without completely losing it.
detail.reply: I’m here to listen. It’s okay to feel overwhelmed. How did you first start to process your grief?

detail.transcript: I got the promotion I wanted and instead of being happy I just feel like they are going to work out I cannot do it.
detail.reply: You wanted the promotion, but now the weight of it feels overwhelming. Does the fear of failure feel louder than the pride of success?

detail.transcript: I have been so lonely since I moved here. I go whole weekends without speaking to anybody.
detail.reply: It sounds like loneliness has been heavy lately. Do you ever feel like you're missing something when you're alone?

detail.transcript: I said something unkind to my partner last night and I have been sitting with how it landed ever since.
detail.reply: You’ve been holding space for what you said. That takes courage. How did it feel when you realized the weight of your words?

detail.transcript: Work has been brutal. I missed a deadline and my boss was furious and I do not think I handled it well.
detail.reply: I heard how work has been tough. Missing a deadline must have felt overwhelming. Did you feel like you had any support at all during the chaos?

detail.transcript: I keep starting things and abandoning them halfway and I am starting to think that is just who I am.
detail.reply: It sounds like you're feeling stuck in a cycle of starting and leaving things. Can you tell me what keeps you from finishing what you begin?

detail.transcript: My friend told me she is moving abroad and I am happy for her and also quietly devastated.
detail.reply: It’s natural to feel both joy and loss when someone you care about leaves. How did you first realize you were attached to her?

detail.transcript: I went for a long walk this evening without my phone and it is the calmest I have felt in weeks.
detail.reply: That sounds like a moment of peace. Did you notice anything else about the walk or the feeling that came with it?

detail.transcript: I am so angry at my brother I could scream, and I know if I call him I will say something I regret.
detail.reply: I hear how heavy that feeling is. You’re carrying a lot right now. What does it feel like when you’re alone with those thoughts?

detail.transcript: I have been pretending I am fine at work for about three months and I am tired of the performance.
detail.reply: It sounds like you've been carrying a lot. How did you start pretending everything was okay?

detail.transcript: My therapist is on leave for a month and I did not realise how much I had been leaning on those sessions.
detail.reply: It’s quiet now without the regular check-ins. How have you been filling the space they left?

detail.transcript: I turned thirty last week and I keep doing this thing where I audit my whole life against where I thought I would be.
detail.reply: It’s easy to feel like you’re falling short when you’re comparing your life to your expectations. What surprised you most about where you are now?

detail.transcript: Someone I barely know was really kind to me today and it almost undid me, which feels embarrassing to admit.
detail.reply: It’s rare to feel that deeply for someone you don’t know well—thank you for sharing that. Did you feel seen in a way you hadn’t expected?

detail.transcript: I have been avoiding my inbox for four days and the avoiding is now worse than whatever is in there.
detail.reply: It sounds like the avoidance has grown heavier. What did you feel when you first saw the inbox, before you decided to avoid it?

detail.transcript: My landlord is selling the flat and I have to move again and I am so tired of not having somewhere that is mine.
detail.reply: I hear how tired you are of not having a place that feels like yours. It’s hard to keep moving. What does it feel like when you finally settle somewhere?

detail.transcript: I had a good day. Nothing special happened. I just want to say that out loud because it has been a while.
detail.reply: It’s nice to hear that. Sometimes just saying things out loud can feel like a small victory. What made the day feel good, even if nothing much happened?

detail.transcript: I keep comparing myself to people I went to university with and it is making me miserable and I cannot stop.
detail.reply: It sounds heavy to carry those comparisons around. How do you usually feel when you notice yourself doing this?

detail.transcript: My dad and I spoke properly for the first time in about two years and I do not know what to do with the feeling.
detail.reply: It’s strange how silence can feel like a language of its own. Did you feel any shift in the space between you two, even if it was just a breath?
